topic: Agent Trajectory Monitor: Watching Tool Calls and Token Spend in Real Time

key_points: Trajectory evaluation assesses the sequence of steps, tool calls, and decisions an agent takes, not just the final output
An ordered action log records the full sequence of reasoning, tool calls, and observations
Five dimensions: tool-call precision (right tool + right args), step efficiency (calls vs minimum needed, loops/retries), plan adherence, action safety, and a reference trajectory
Output-only scoring can't tell a reliable agent from one that reaches the right answer by chance
Build a grounded reference trajectory from real business logic to score the process as a baseline
Giving an agent DB access without monitoring tool calls, context growth, and token spend creates an 'autonomous denial-of-service engine'
An autonomous agent fails by hallucinating parameters, getting stuck in recursive retry loops, exhausting its context window, or burning API token budgets
2026 shift: teams deploy autonomous SRE agents that act on infrastructure (spin up read replicas, terminate blocking queries, modify autoscaling)
CloudWatch and Datadog evolved built-in generative AI observability
Monitoring an agent is fundamentally different than monitoring an application (code execution is no longer deterministic)
AI agents use 5-30x more tokens per task than standard chatbots — untracked usage drives budget overruns
OpenAI Chat Completions requires stream_options: {"include_usage": true} to return aggregate token usage in the final stream chunk
Track via provider usage APIs and application telemetry, or centralized MCP Gateway + Agent Monitor for governance
Token optimization can cut costs in workloads with duplicated context, unnecessary loops, or avoidable high-cost model calls
Shadow AI detection: agents running outside governed infrastructure consume tokens without attribution or audit trails
In production AI environments, cost visibility is a design constraint, not a byproduct
Measure token consumption per agent and per tool call, cap token spend per workflow, instrument real-time budgets tied to business KPIs
Build cost models for each tool and route, implement alerting when thresholds are breached, enforce budget-aware routing for fallbacks
Cost driven by token usage, tool calls, API rate limits, and data transfer
Token counting must align with the exact model and prompt structure used in production, not just raw input length
An AI agent run can look successful while doing the wrong work — calling the right tool with wrong arguments, entering a loop, or following a slow path
APM traces capture errors and latency but stop at the infrastructure boundary; prompt-only logs miss routing choices and context changes
A single request can trigger many model and tool calls, leading to higher latency and costs
Telemetry, traces, metrics, and evals are the four pillars of AI agent observability
Use AI agent observability with both single agents and multi-agent systems

stats.fact: AI agents consume 5-30x more tokens per task than standard chatbots
Even as per-token costs fall, overall inference costs keep rising because agentic workloads consume substantially more tokens and perform more tasks than chatbot interactions
OpenAI Chat Completions requires stream_options: {"include_usage": true} to return aggregate token usage in a final stream chunk
In 2026 teams deploy autonomous SRE agents that act on infrastructure with read/write production access via secure toolchains
A single agent request can trigger many model and tool calls, leading to higher latency and costs

angles: Position a trajectory monitor as the missing 'flight recorder' for AI agents — replaying every tool call, token spend, and decision in real time
Frame the cost angle: agents burning 5-30x more tokens than chatbots means real-time token monitoring is a budget requirement, not a nice-to-have
Focus on distinguishing 'right answer by chance' from reliable agents via tool-call precision and step efficiency — a trajectory monitor exposes this
Highlight real-time signals: detecting recursive retry loops, context window exhaustion, duplicated context, and wrong-argument tool calls before they burn budget
Practical how-to: which metrics to watch (tool-call precision, step efficiency, token/step, latency), where to get them (stream_options usage, provider APIs, MCP gateway), and how to alert
